research_question: For fixed synthetic graduate-student scenarios, does a structured score combining skill coverage, academic-field compatibility and stated career preferences improve Precision@3 and NDCG@3 over skill-only ranking?
hypothesis: Additional compatibility attributes may improve ordering when skill overlap alone leaves tied or contextually unsuitable opportunities; improvement is not assumed for every profile.
preference_components: Equal weights for opportunity type and work-mode compatibility
fit_or_tuning: None: fixed attribute scoring; no supervised model, learned weights or validation search
input_design: 6 manually constructed graduate profiles and 12 fictional opportunities, with all 72 labeled pairs; labels and rationales fixed before scores. No live job postings or real student data.

label_rubric.0: No useful match in the intended scenario
label_rubric.1: Transferable or partial fit, including a material skill, domain or stated-preference limitation
label_rubric.2: Strong intended role fit with substantial required-skill and contextual compatibility

limitations: Author-defined grades share concepts with the scoring rule and are not independent judgments. This is a constructed diagnostic benchmark, not held-out evidence of real student utility.
